question: What is the primary parasitic infection diagnosed using a skin snip procedure?
explanation: Skin snips specifically target the dermal microfilariae of Onchocerca volvulus to confirm river blindness. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h1)

question: Why are skin snips typically performed on patients living near fast-flowing rivers?

options.A: Parasitic worms migrate downward toward water sources at night
options.B: The river water is used to clean the surgical site before cutting
options.C: High humidity near rivers prevents wound healing complications
options.D: Blackflies transmitting the parasite breed in fast-flowing water

explanation: Simulium blackflies require rapidly moving streams to complete their breeding cycle, putting nearby populations at high risk. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h1)

question: Which surgical tool is commonly used to excise the tiny tissue sample during a skin snip?
explanation: A small scalpel blade or specialized punch is required to shave off a superficial piece of skin without drawing deep blood. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is the main reason for maintaining strict aseptic technique during a skin snip?

options.A: To ensure the microfilariae do not escape the slide
options.B: To stop the local anesthetic from wearing off early
options.C: To keep the microscope lenses from getting foggy
options.D: To prevent secondary bacterial wound infections

explanation: Any breach of the skin barrier creates an entry point for environmental pathogens, making sterile prep essential. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why must the nurse or clinician avoid grabbing deep subcutaneous fat with the forceps during the procedure?

options.A: The laboratory microscope cannot penetrate deep tissue layers
options.B: It causes excessive bleeding and is unnecessary for finding microfilariae
options.C: The microfilariae only live inside the deep muscle tissue instead
options.D: Local anesthetic cannot numb fat tissue effectively

explanation: Microfilariae reside in the superficial dermis, so deep tissue collection only increases trauma and bleeding risk without clinical benefit. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h3)

question: What is the typical diameter size of the skin tissue sample obtained during a snip?
explanation: A very small superficial snip is all that is needed to examine dermal fluid under the microscope. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h3)

question: What happens to the skin tissue sample immediately after it is excised from the patient?

options.A: It is stitched back onto the patient as an autograft
options.B: It is immediately burned in an incinerator to destroy pathogens
options.C: It is frozen solid in a liquid nitrogen container
options.D: It is placed in a liquid medium to let microfilariae emerge

explanation: The worms need moisture to crawl out of the dermal tissue matrix so they can be identified under a microscope. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h4)

question: How long are samples sometimes incubated to check for delayed migration of microfilariae?
explanation: An incubation period of up to 24 hours ensures that slower-migrating microfilariae are counted before declaring a test negative. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h4)

question: A patient who underwent a skin snip and received ivermectin develops fever, swollen lymph nodes, and a rash. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A severe bacterial infection from dirty instruments
options.B: An allergic reaction to the adhesive bandage
options.C: A Mazzotti reaction from dying microfilariae
options.D: Normal systemic rejection of the skin graft

explanation: Mass destruction of microfilariae by microfilaricidal drugs triggers an immune response known as the Mazzotti reaction. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h5)

question: Which instruction is most important for a patient caring for a skin snip site at home?

options.A: Apply medicated skin bleaching cream daily
options.B: Keep the small bandage clean and dry
options.C: Scrub the wound vigorously with a sponge
options.D: Soak the area in river water twice a day

explanation: Standard minor wound care requires keeping the site clean and dry to prevent secondary bacterial invasion. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h5)
